original_statement: For every uniform Boolean core g with a=1-Eg>=11/16 and independent compatible point-control blocks of common width s>=0 and exclusive widths r,t>=1, F=1+A_s(A_r OR A_t)(g-1) has a finite control-first stopping tree with exactly zero strict threshold-4 bad-node odd-face credit before the core terminal. Every queried node has B_v<4d_v for d_v>0. With u=2^-s,p=2^-r,q=2^-t,beta=p+q-pq, I_ctrl=u a[s beta+r p(1-q)+t q(1-p)], I_leaf=u beta I(g), H_leaf=u beta H(g). Thus H(F)<7I_ctrl+H_leaf, genuine minority/KL debt plus H_leaf<=4I_ctrl+H_leaf, and its full 3mu/ln2 allowance plus H_leaf<9I_ctrl+H_leaf. A more general sufficient local condition for a fresh point event against any independent residual event of probability q is a(1-q)>e/8. If g selects any bent sign on even k>=4 bits or its one-vertex flip, H(g)/I(g)<3 and therefore H(F)<7I(F), J+terminal<=4I(F), full sufficient KL ledger<9I(F), uniformly in all widths and k. Common coordinates and the shared core are paid once. Additional one-separator theorem: for all independent fresh point blocks W,U,V of widths L,R,T>=1, one fair bit X and independent balanced Boolean g, let A=XU OR XV OR WUV, F=1+A(g-1), p=2^-L,q=2^-R,r=2^-T, beta=q+r-qr,eta=pqr,pi=(beta+eta)/2,e=beta-eta. Query X first, then resolve WUV or U OR V, stopping at a constant or g. Every descendant control node is strictly threshold-4-good; no root-goodness is assumed. d_X=e/2, Jrem=[(L+R+T)eta+R q(1-r)+T r(1-q)]/2, I(F)=d_X+Jrem+pi I(g), terminal entropy=pi H(g). The root face cost is exactly Jrem+e I(g)/2 and Q_bad<=Jrem+pi I(g)=I(F)-d_X. One marked reserve, consumed before descent and never renewed, proves H(F)<=(5+2/ln2)(d_X+Jrem)+pi H(g)+e I(g)/2. Retained genuine minority/KL bill is <=5(d_X+Jrem)+pi H(g)+e I(g)/2; adding its 3mu/ln2 allowance replaces 5 by 5+3/ln2. If H(g)<=C0 I(g), H(F)<=max(5+2/ln2,C0+1)I(F). For g=z times a fair selector between any bent sign on even k>=4 bits and its one-vertex flip, H(F)<8I(F), retained J+terminal<=5I(F), and full sufficient KL ledger<10I(F), uniformly in L,R,T,k. This does not assert repeated-separator reserve ownership or arbitrary-core FEI. Additional whole-block theorem: for EVERY Boolean G,H on the same uniform data cube, s>=1 fresh point controls, alpha=2^-s, gamma=P(G!=H), F=G+A_s(H-G), query controls to resolution and stop at actual G or H. Let I_S=2s alpha gamma, I_T=(1-alpha)I(G)+alpha I(H), H_T=(1-alpha)H(G)+alpha H(H), R=2alpha(1-alpha)I(GH). Then I(F)=I_S+I_T, R<=2I_T, and E_B<=2(1-2alpha)I_S+4alpha gamma(1-alpha)[log2(1/gamma)+1/ln2], with gamma=0 interpreted continuously. H(F)-H_T<=(11/2)I_S+R; genuine retained minority/KL debt<= (5/2)I_S+R; adding3mu/ln2 gives<=7I_S+R. Strict scalar-rate slack holds when I_S>0. Each physical data coordinate reserves at most2alpha times its inactive-terminal influence and2(1-alpha) times its active-terminal influence, marked once for the whole block and never reissued at selector descendants. If H(G)<=C_G I(G), H(H)<=C_H I(H), then H(F)<=max(11/2,C_G+2alpha,C_H+2(1-alpha))I(F). For any bent sign on even m>=4 bits and its actual one-vertex flip, both multiplied by one shared independent balancing sign z, the switched family has H<(11/2)I, retained J+terminal<=4I and full sufficient KL ledger<7I, uniformly in m,s. Fresh width-t point activation of that balanced family has H<6I and I=2^-t[I(F)+t]->0 for fixed m,s as t grows. No bound on arbitrary localized bad-face credit or repeatedly renewed nested terminal reserves is asserted.
